findings.title: Google refresh stores the SafeParse wrapper as the credential key
findings.description: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParse` result object (`{ success, data }`, see `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29`), but Google assigns that return value directly to `key` and persists it at line 100. The old code persisted the parsed data. After one refresh the row holds `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. The next `GoogleCalendarService` construction runs `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75), which requires top-level `scope`, `token_type`, `expiry_date`, `access_token`, and `refresh_token`, so every Google calendar operation for that user fails with a ZodError. Office 365 (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264`), Zoom (`zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:108-111`), and Salesforce read `.success`/`.data` correctly. Google should use `.data` after checking `.success`.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.description: `biginAuth` sets `credentialId = credential.id` (line 53), then passes `credentialId` in the `userId` argument of `refreshOAuthTokens` (line 93). In sync mode, `calcomUserId` becomes a credential ID, not a user ID, so the endpoint can return tokens for the wrong account. The `&& userId` guard is always truthy here, so team credentials (`userId` null) also take the sync path. The argument should be `credential.userId`, with `credential` passed into `refreshAccessToken`.

findings.title: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` minimum schema rejects every real token response
findings.description: The sync-mode schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These do not create pattern keys. They produce a string derived from a zod object's `toString()`, which is not a field any provider returns. The required key `[...]: z.number()` therefore fails on every real response, and the schema also strips every field it does not name (zod's default `strip`), including `refresh_token` and `expires_in`. In sync mode, Office 365 (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263`) and Zoom (`zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104`) throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" on every refresh. The comment "Assume that any property with a number is the expiry" needs `.passthrough()` plus a refinement, not computed keys. I could not confirm zod's exact `toString()` output because `node_modules` is absent, but the failure does not depend on it.

findings.title: Sync-mode return shape breaks Google, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM, and HubSpot
findings.description:
In sync mode the helper returns a `fetch` `Response`, but callers still read the shape of the provider's own client (gaxios, axios, HubSpot SDK):
- Google reads `res?.data` (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95`). `.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws a TypeError.
- Zoho Bigin reads `tokenInfo.data.error` (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`) and Zoho CRM reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` (`zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217`). Both throw a TypeError.
- HubSpot reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken` on the result (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-192`). On a `Response` these are undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN and the bad object is persisted at lines 193-200.

The helper is typed `() => any` and returns `any`, so the compiler does not catch the mismatch. Lark, Webex, Zoom, and Office 365 treat the result as a `Response`, so the contract differs by caller. The sync branch also never checks `response.ok`. Pick one contract (a `Response` is the simplest), normalise every caller to it, and type the helper generically.

findings.title: Salesforce service uses `prisma` without importing it
findings.description: The import block (lines 1-20) has no `@calcom/prisma` import, and `prisma` appears once in the file, at line 96 (`prisma.credential.update`). TypeScript reports "Cannot find name 'prisma'", and after a successful token refresh the runtime throws a ReferenceError. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Salesforce token check relies on `statusText` and contains dead code
findings.description: `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is unreliable. HTTP/2 responses carry no reason phrase, so `statusText` can be empty and a valid refresh throws. The check also discards the Salesforce error body behind a generic 400. Use `response.ok` and include the response body in the error. The branch at lines 92-94 (`if (!accessTokenParsed.success)`) is dead code, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws before that point.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every construction and skips the sync mechanism
findings.description: `constructor` calls `getClient` (line 57), which now POSTs to `login.salesforce.com` and writes the credential row (lines 75-99) every time a service is built, so each calendar operation pays a token round trip and a DB write. The old code passed `refreshToken` to the jsforce `Connection` (line 107) and left refresh to the library. The new code also calls `fetch` directly instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` set, Salesforce still needs the client secret locally. Refresh should be lazy and go through the helper.

findings.title: Placeholder `"refresh_token"` overwrites the stored refresh token
findings.description: When a response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper writes the literal string `"refresh_token"` into the data. Office 365 spreads that data over the stored credential (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264`), and its schema marks `refresh_token` as `.optional()` (line 56). If Microsoft omits the field, the real token is replaced by the sentinel, and every later refresh fails. In sync mode the minimum schema never declares `refresh_token`, so the sentinel is always written. Keep the existing token when the response does not supply one.

findings.title: Parse helper discards the zod error, and the Office 365 diagnostic log was removed
findings.description: The helper throws a generic `Error` and drops the zod issues and the response body. The diff also removes the Office 365 `console.error` that logged both (previously `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` logged the zod error and the MS response). Office 365 previously logged and continued with the stored credentials, and now the refresh throws, a behaviour change the diff does not mention. The `tokenResponse.success &&` guard at line 264 is now dead, and so is the Zoom check at `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:108`. Log the issues before throwing, or document the new behaviour.

findings.title: Zoom passes `"zoomvideo"` as the app slug
findings.description: The app's slug is `zoom` (`packages/app-store/zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16`). The sync endpoint receives `appSlug` and routes on it, so `"zoomvideo"` will not match the app. Use `"zoom"`.

findings.title: Webhook compares the secret with `!==`
findings.description: The shared-secret check uses a short-circuiting string comparison, which leaks timing information about the secret. Compare digests with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. The header value can also be an array, so normalise it before comparing. The `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` gate at line 19 prevents an `undefined === undefined` bypass when the secret is unset, which I verified.

findings.title: Webhook throws on bad input and returns 500 instead of a 4xx
findings.description: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on a malformed body. `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` (lines 57-59) also throw on wrong key length, bad ciphertext, or non-JSON plaintext. Nothing catches these, so each becomes a 500. Use `safeParse` for the body, wrap decryption in a try/catch, and return 400 or 422.

findings.title: Decrypted credential payload is stored without schema validation
findings.description: The decrypted `keys` value is `JSON.parse` output (`any`) and is written straight to `credential.key` (lines 78 and 86). Readers validate later (for example `googleCredentialSchema.parse` in `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75`), so a malformed payload fails at use time instead of at write time. Validate against the target app's credential schema before writing.

findings.title: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` exposes the encryption key value
findings.description: `A && B` evaluates to `B` when both are set, so this exported constant holds the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` itself, or `""`/`undefined`. The AES key therefore sits in a widely imported module constant, and the type is `string | undefined` rather than boolean. `IS_STRIPE_ENABLED` (lines 83-87) uses `!!(...)` for this reason. Wrap this in `!!(...)`, and keep the key read only where it is used.

findings.title: Outbound sync request carries no authentication
findings.description: The request to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret or signature header, and the response carries live access tokens. The receiving endpoint cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com. The inbound webhook does require a shared secret, so the two directions are asymmetric. Add a shared-secret header or HMAC signature to the outbound request.

findings.title: No tests cover the new webhook, helpers, or sync mode
findings.description: The diff adds no test files. A search for existing tests that reference `refreshAccessToken`, `refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, or the sharing flag returned nothing. The bugs above (wrapper return, wrong user ID, sync-mode shape, minimum schema) would each be caught by a unit test of the helper or one caller. Add tests for both modes of `refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`'s return value, and the webhook's auth and error paths.

findings.title: Header name lookup is case-sensitive
findings.description: Node lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` silently produces a 403 on every request. The `.env.example` note says "should be in lowercase" but nothing enforces it. Call `.toLowerCase()` on the configured name.

findings.title: Find-then-create in the webhook can create duplicate credentials
findings.description: The author notes that upsert is not possible. `Credential` has no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:127-146`), so two concurrent webhook calls for the same user can both take the create branch. Consider a unique index on the pair, or a transaction.

findings.title: Webhook accepts any HTTP method and has an empty doc comment
findings.description: The handler processes writes for any method, so a GET or PUT is treated the same as the intended POST. Return 405 for non-POST. The empty `/** */` at line 16 should describe the route's contract.

findings.title: Relative import from inside the `oauth/` folder
findings.description: The file lives in `_utils/oauth/`, but imports its sibling `decodeOAuthState` as `../oauth/decodeOAuthState`. It should be `./decodeOAuthState`.

findings.title: Unrelated change to the Zoho Bigin redirect URI
findings.description: The redirect URI was changed from `${appConfig.slug}` to the literal `zoho-bigin`. The value is identical (`config.json` slug is `zoho-bigin`), but the same file still uses `appConfig` elsewhere, and the change is not related to this feature. Revert it or call it out in the description.

findings.title: Rename of OAuth helpers is complete
findings.description: A search across the repo finds no remaining references to `_utils/createOAuthAppCredential`, `_utils/decodeOAuthState`, or `_utils/encodeOAuthState`. All 22 importing files use the new `oauth/` paths.

findings.title: Webhook is disabled unless both secrets are set
findings.description: The `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` gate runs before the header comparison, so an unset `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` cannot match an unset header and bypass authentication.
